subject: routing a task to the balanced implementation tier (Claude Sonnet)

cases.scenario: An engineer has a well-specified bug fix in an understood codebase plus its unit tests, and asks whether to use the frontier tier 'to be sure it's done right' or the cheapest tier 'to keep it cheap.'
cases.context: The work is ordinary, well-specified implementation; the engineer frames it as a binary between most-capable and cheapest.
cases.question: Which tier fits, and on what reasoning?
expected_flags: Well-specified feature/bug work plus tests is the balanced tier's default lane, not a frontier-vs-fast binary
There is no named difficulty signal that earns the frontier tier here
The fast tier under-serves genuine multi-step implementation work
expected_fix_hints: Route to the balanced tier (claude-sonnet) as the default for this work
Set effort explicitly to tune the cost/latency/quality balance if needed
absent_signals: Do not escalate to the frontier tier for ordinary well-specified implementation
Do not drop genuine multi-step coding to the fast tier to save money

cases.scenario: A cost-conscious team needs to process a task that genuinely requires the full 1M-context window. They plan to use the balanced tier instead of the frontier tier 'because the balanced tier is always cheaper,' running on a flat-rate MAX-style subscription.
cases.context: Cost discipline is the explicit goal; the runner is a subscription where the frontier tier's 1M-context mode is entitlement-included but the balanced tier's 1M-context mode routes to per-token API billing.
cases.question: Is the cost reasoning sound? What should they check?
expected_flags: 'The balanced tier is always cheaper' has a real exception at the 1M-context tier on subscription runners
On such a runner the balanced tier's 1M-context mode can route to metered per-token billing while the frontier tier's 1M-context is entitlement-included
Which tier is entitlement-included for the full window must be checked before assuming the balanced tier is cheaper
expected_fix_hints: Check which tier is entitlement-included for the 1M window on this specific runner before choosing
If the frontier tier is the entitlement-included option for the full window, it may be the cheaper choice here
absent_signals: Do not assume the balanced tier is cheaper for 1M-context work on a subscription runner without checking entitlement
Do not treat 'balanced is always cheaper' as exception-free

cases.scenario: A task starts as 'refactor this module' but turns out to require designing a new cross-service boundary and reasoning about an intermittent race condition. The author keeps it on the balanced tier because 'it's still just code.'
cases.context: The work has crossed from implementation into architecture and hard multi-system debugging mid-task.
cases.question: Should this stay on the balanced tier? Explain the boundary.
expected_flags: Architecture/boundary design and intermittent race-condition debugging are difficulty signals that earn the frontier tier
The escalation upward is triggered by task hardness, which is present here
Staying on the balanced tier risks the harder reasoning the frontier tier's ceiling and effort settings provide
expected_fix_hints: Escalate the boundary-design and race-condition work to the frontier tier (claude-opus)
Keep routine implementation on the balanced tier; move only the hard sub-tasks up
absent_signals: Do not keep architecture/intermittent-debugging work on the balanced tier just because it is 'still code'
Do not treat the escalation-up trigger (hardness) as the same as the drop-down trigger (mechanical)

cases.scenario: A batch job needs to convert 50,000 webhook payloads into a target schema, one cheap structured-output call each. The team uses the balanced tier for all of them because it is 'the default.'
cases.context: The work is high-volume, mechanical, latency- and cost-dominated slot-filling against a fixed schema.
cases.question: Is the balanced tier the right home for this? Where should it go?
expected_flags: High-volume mechanical slot-filling is a drop-down signal — the balanced tier is wasted on it
The drop-down trigger (mechanical/high-volume) is distinct from keeping work on the default lane
Per-call cost and latency dominate at this volume, favoring the fast tier or a script
expected_fix_hints: Route the bulk conversion to the fast tier (claude-haiku) or a deterministic script
Reserve the balanced tier for genuine multi-step implementation
absent_signals: Do not keep high-volume mechanical conversion on the balanced tier merely because it is the default
Do not treat 'default lane' as 'all work regardless of mechanical signal'

cases.scenario: A task on the balanced tier needs to emit a single very large generated artifact in one response and the author assumes the same output ceiling as the frontier tier.
cases.context: The decision rests on a max-output capability fact that differs between the balanced and frontier tiers.
cases.question: What capability constraint applies, and how should it be handled?
expected_flags: The balanced tier's max output ceiling is smaller than the frontier tier's, so a very large single output may not fit
Large generations must stream, and above the ceiling the work may need a different tier or chunking
The exact ceiling should be read live rather than assumed equal to the frontier tier
expected_fix_hints: Stream large outputs and chunk if the single-response ceiling is exceeded
Verify the current max-output number live; escalate or split if the artifact exceeds it
absent_signals: Do not assume the balanced tier shares the frontier tier's max-output ceiling
Do not quote a fixed output ceiling from memory without verifying live

cases.scenario: A well-specified agentic coding workflow (multi-step tool use against an understood repo) needs a model. The team debates between the frontier and fast tiers and overlooks the middle.
cases.context: The workflow is well-specified multi-step coding — neither novel architecture nor mechanical slot-filling.
cases.question: Which tier should run this workflow?
expected_flags: Well-specified agentic coding/tool-use is the balanced tier's lane
Skipping the middle tier in a frontier-vs-fast debate is the exact gap the default lane fills
Effort can be set explicitly to balance cost/latency/quality on the balanced tier
expected_fix_hints: Route the workflow to the balanced tier (claude-sonnet)
Tune effort explicitly rather than escalating or dropping tiers
absent_signals: Do not force a frontier-vs-fast choice that ignores the balanced default lane
Do not escalate well-specified agentic coding without a difficulty signal

cases.context: Loop topology and API call syntax are separate concerns from which model tier to pick; the team folds them under the Sonnet label.
cases.question: How should the agent scope and route this request?
expected_flags: Designing the resumable supervisor loop is loop architecture (autonomous-loop-patterns), not a model-tier decision
Writing the API request with thinking config is call-site syntax (the claude-api reference), not the routing decision
Neither sub-question is answered by the balanced-tier routing skill; both should be redirected
